correctness.rationale: The scalar Richardson stability function has coefficients 1, -1, 1/2, 0, -3/8 through order four. At graph distances 1 and 2 the first offdiagonal terms are positive; at distance 3 the leading coefficient is -(3/8)(L^4)uv. Every four-edge walk and three-edge path appears in the exact neighbor-set identity derived in RESULT.md. Deleting all but one bridge raises that coefficient, and each remaining vertex contributes at most max(0,ab-2). Evaluating the complete possible neighbor-set sizes proves (L^4)uv<=-1 through order 9 and <=4 through order 10. The ten-vertex witness has diameter 3 and (L^4)uv=4, hence a negative leading term. The nine-vertex bound is attained. The standalone exact verifier checks both witnesses, four exact resolvent signs, and 2499 independently generated graph-pair formula comparisons. Finite tests are explicitly not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The exact minimum graph size and the sharp fourth-Laplacian inequality are not the original backward-Euler extrapolation formula or its known scalar positivity radius. Lawson--Morris 1977 equations (2.1)-(2.6) and page 9 exhibit the same method and known scalar sign issue; Constantinescu--Sandu 2008 Section 2 develops general extrapolation stability, not a graph order threshold. A published scalar Richardson positivity investigation gives scalar thresholds, but the exact 9/10 graph size separation and coefficient bound require new graph combinatorics. The accessible related mathematical history includes a 13-vertex diameter-three obstruction but not its minimality; the new theorem determines the sharp 10-vertex minimum. General novelty cannot be certified by searches alone.

value.rationale: The minimum size of a graph exhibiting immediate violation of positivity is a natural obstruction invariant for a high-order heat integrator. The result supplies an exact safe finite-size cutoff, a sharp universal distance-three fourth-Laplacian inequality, and extremal graphs on both sides; it is not merely a smaller witness or a numerical census. This can guide testing of higher-order resolvent combinations on modest networks. The claim is deliberately local and unit-weight only.
